title: Investigating the predictability of postoperative pain by intraoperative nociception monitoring and EEG
summary:
The amount of pain medication administered during anesthesia plays an important role in how you feel after an operation. Both overdoses and underdoses can have undesirable consequences. For example, while an overdose can lead to increased nausea, an underdose can lead to increased pain even after the operation. Various devices have been developed in recent years to reduce such undesirable consequences and improve the accuracy of painkiller dosing during anesthesia. However, it is not yet known which values displayed by these devices reliably indicate over- or underdosing. 

In order to investigate this and to enable a more precise dosage of painkillers during anesthesia in the future, we are conducting this scientific study. In this study, we investigate and compare various monitoring devices that could be used to predict during anesthesia the pain and adverse effects that will occur in the short and long term after an operation.

interventions.name:
Patients undergoing elective surgery under total intravenous general anesthesia are included.
The reaction to painful and non-painful measures is observed before, during and after anesthesia.  In addition, the frontal EEG, skin conductivity and the dosage of propofol and remifentanil are continuous

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
2. patients with an ASA status I to III (according to the American Society of  Anesthesiologists)
3. planned elective surgery under total intravenous general anesthesia  (TIVA)
4. planned securing of the airway by tracheal intubation
5. ability to give written informed consent
6. presence of written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. required rapid sequence induction
2. taking antipsychotics and antidepressants
3. chronic pain disorder with current opioid medication
4. inability to answer the preoperative questionnaire unaided
5. pre-existing pupillary anomaly or condition after pupil-altering eye surgery 
6. BMI >35 kg/m2
